name: Chloe Wright

participation_history.notes: Great session. Chloe walked us through her full checkout experience with real examples.

notes: She/her. Shops online 3-4x per week, mostly on mobile. Highly opinionated about checkout UX — has abandoned many carts. Very articulate participant.

session_insights.raw_notes: Chloe shared that she almost always abandons checkout if she has to create an account. Said she has 'account fatigue' from too many sign-ups. The guest checkout option on our app is hidden below the login form which she never noticed - she thought it wasn't possible. Big moment: when asked to complete a test purchase she spent 40 seconds looking for an apple pay or google pay button - said 'I never type my card details on my phone, it's too fiddly and I don't trust it'. Also flagged that the order summary disappears when you scroll down on the payment screen - she lost track of what she was buying. Quote: 'If I have to type my card number on a tiny keyboard I'm already annoyed before I've bought anything'. Said she'd recommend the app to friends if checkout was faster.
key_insights: Guest checkout option is invisible — placed below the login form, users assume it doesn't exist
Strong preference for one-tap payment (Apple Pay / Google Pay) on mobile — typing card details feels fiddly and untrustworthy
Order summary should remain visible (sticky) during the payment step — users lose context when it disappears on scroll
Account creation fatigue is real — forced sign-up is the primary abandonment trigger for frequent online shoppers
follow_up_items: Redesign guest checkout CTA — make it equal prominence to the login option
Prioritise Apple Pay / Google Pay integration in the next sprint
Make order summary sticky on the payment screen
Chloe is happy to review a redesigned prototype — flag for concept testing round
quotes: If I have to type my card number on a tiny keyboard I'm already annoyed before I've bought anything
I didn't even know guest checkout was an option — I thought you had to sign up

name: Marcus Thompson
notes: He/him. Shops online once or twice a month, mostly for considered purchases. Reads reviews carefully before buying. Good contrast to power-user participants.

name: Anika Patel
notes: She/her. 22 years old. Shops almost exclusively on mobile. Price-compares across apps before buying. Heavy social commerce user (TikTok Shop, Instagram).

session_insights.raw_notes:
anika session - checkout flow proj
talked for about 45 mins
she shops mostly on mobile, does a lot of impulse buys
biggest thing: she always checks the return policy before buying but its REALLY hard to find on mobile
like she has to scroll forever to the footer
also payment - she uses apple pay for everything but loads of sites dont support it
when that happens she just... leaves. abandons the cart
she mentioned she had a bad experience last month, tried to buy shoes, couldnt find return policy, 
then apple pay wasnt available, ended up going to competitor
oh also she said the checkout progress bar is helpful - she likes knowing how many steps left
wants to know: will guest checkout save her details for next time? she doesnt like creating accounts
follow up: send her the prototype link for mobile checkout flow
also she said she knows 2 other friends who have same frustrations, ask if she can refer them??
key_insights: Return policy visibility is a pre-purchase blocker on mobile: Anika actively seeks return policy information before buying but finds it buried in the footer, requiring excessive scrolling on mobile devices
Missing Apple Pay support directly causes cart abandonment: When preferred payment method (Apple Pay) isn't available, Anika leaves immediately rather than entering card details manually
Competitor defection happens when multiple friction points compound: The combination of hard-to-find return policy AND missing Apple Pay caused Anika to abandon and purchase from a competitor instead
Checkout progress indicators provide reassurance: Visible step indicators help users understand remaining effort and reduce anxiety during checkout
Guest checkout expectations are unclear: Users like Anika want guest checkout but are uncertain whether their details will be saved for future purchases, creating hesitation around account creation
follow_up_items: Send Anika the mobile checkout flow prototype link for feedback
Ask if she can refer her 2 friends with similar frustrations for additional research sessions
Explore: What would make guest checkout more appealing? Does she want optional detail-saving without full account creation?
Probe deeper on Apple Pay abandonment: Does she ever complete purchase with manual card entry, or is it always abandonment?
quotes: When that happens she just... leaves. Abandons the cart
Will guest checkout save her details for next time?

name: Noah Fitzgerald
notes: He/him. Tries new apps early. Notices technical details others miss — broken animations, slow load states, inconsistent UI. Useful for finding edge cases.

session_insights.raw_notes:
mcp test session - noah jenkins - checkout flow project
~40 min session, ran a bit over

noah shops maybe 2-3x per month online, mostly electronics and hobby stuff
main friction: saved cards stop working after a while?? he has to re-enter them
also said he always checks if site has paypal before he adds to cart
if no paypal he usually doesn't bother unless it's something he really wants

interesting: he described the progress bar on checkout as "a loading bar for my money"
thought it was funny but actually said it helps him not abandon

he doesn't read return policies - just assumes big sites are fine
buys based on delivery speed, same/next day is a dealbreaker criteria for him

got distracted talking about his last bad experience - bought something,
no confirmation email came, thought it failed, bought again, ended up with 2
follow up on: does he want sms vs email confirmation?
and: would saved address/card across sessions change his behaviour?
key_insights: Payment method availability (specifically PayPal) is a gate-check before adding to cart — Noah will abandon before even starting if his preferred payment isn't available
Saved payment credentials degrading over time creates repeat friction — cards 'stop working' forcing re-entry, which erodes the value of account creation
Visual progress indicators during checkout reduce abandonment — Noah specifically cited the progress bar as helping him complete purchases
Delivery speed (same/next day) is a hard requirement that influences purchase decisions more than price or return policies
Missing order confirmation triggers duplicate purchases — lack of immediate feedback led Noah to re-purchase, creating a support burden and trust issue
follow_up_items: Explore preference for SMS vs email order confirmation — which channel does he trust/check faster?
Test whether persistent saved addresses and cards across sessions would reduce his checkout friction and increase purchase frequency
Dig deeper into the 'saved cards stop working' issue — is this session expiry, tokenization, or security re-verification?
Understand threshold for 'really wanting' something that overrides lack of PayPal — what product/price triggers override his usual abandonment?
quotes: a loading bar for my money
